component_findings.current_continuity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--zig): A community-maintained, continuously updated GitHub list specifically catalogs companies and non-profit organizations reporting production Zig usage, indicating organized community tracking of adoption beyond the few headline names.
component_findings.deployment_depth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--zig): Ghostty is cited alongside TigerBeetle as a real, continuing production Zig deployment in 2026 comparative analyses.
component_findings.domain_diversity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--zig): TigerBeetle is built entirely in Zig for a distributed, deterministic financial ledger, deployed in production clusters of six replicas across multiple cloud providers; TigerBeetle and Synadia jointly pledged $512,000 to the Zig Software Foundation.

metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Adoption evidence relies partly on company engineering blogs and foundation sponsorship disclosures, which are self-reported by adopters or the foundation rather than independently audited; job-posting counts are a rough proxy and were not used as the sole basis for the score.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.candidate_universe: ziglang.org/learn/tools/ page; VS Code Marketplace search 'zig'; JetBrains Marketplace search 'zig'; zigtools/zls GitHub repo; Zed docs languages/zig page; emacs-lsp lsp-mode zig page

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--zig): Zig has broad, actively-maintained coverage across the major general-purpose editors (VS Code official extension, JetBrains via ZigBrains, Zed, Emacs, plus community Vim/Sublime/Neovim integrations not itemized above) built on a single well-supported official-adjacent language server (ZLS) that covers core IDE features and delegates formatting to the canonical `zig fmt`. Coverage is materially thinner outside editor tooling: there is no Zig-specific debugger (debugging borrows GDB/LLDB or an IDE's native/C++ debugger backend), no broad ecosystem of independent static-analysis or linting tools beyond `zig fmt`/ZLS diagnostics, and pre-1.0 language churn (e.g. the 2026 package-manager overhaul
component_findings.ci_devops: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--zig): Formatting is delivered by the built-in `zig fmt` command and ZLS wraps it directly for editors, so there is a single canonical formatter but no large ecosystem of independent third-party linters comparable to mature mainstream languages.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Popularity/marketplace-listing counts were used only descriptively (which extensions exist and what they support), not as a standalone numeric popularity proxy, per methodology constraints on raw popularity indicators.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.
